name: BancorNetwork v0.6 public safeTransferFrom drains user approvals
summary: BancorNetwork v0.6 exposed safeTransferFrom(token, from, to, value) as a public function that calls token.transferFrom(from, to, value) with no caller check, so anyone could move tokens of any user who had approved the contract. Bancor began rescuing approved balances to its wallet 0x29551fc9 in block 10287175; a front-running bot (EOA 0x052ede4c via 0xea4df374 and 0x01da73c4) outbid the first rescue and in the anchor called 0x5f58058c.safeTransferFrom(BAT, 0x0087c590, 0x01da73c4, 14703.83 BAT). Two bots and two other callers then drained further approvals through 0x5f58058c and its sibling deployment 0x8dfeb86c over 29 more transactions, mostly BNT, DAI, VEE, MKR, BAT and KNC, and sold most of it.
notes: Reset is ContractRegistry 0x52ae12ab's AddressUpdate of 'BancorNetwork' to 0x5f58058c (block 10277001), which routed users, and so their approvals, to it 24 blocks after its deployment (0xef2c15e3, block 10276977). The registry moved on to sibling 0x8dfeb86c (block 10282599, same safeTransferFrom) before the anchor, but approvals already granted to 0x5f58058c stayed exploitable; the fixed network 0x2f9ec37d was registered in 0xcc44634c (block 10287416). 0x923cab01, the first v0.6 deployment, had the same function but no unaffiliated drain went through it.

Affiliation: every call routing tokens to 0x29551fc9 is Bancor's rescue (direct calls from 0xc8021b97, a ConverterRegistry admin since 2019, and 0x14fa61fd, funded by deployer 0xdfee8dc2, plus one-shot rescue contracts they created, first 0xdba03739 at index 4 of the anchor block). The DeFiHackLabs PoC's example 0x4643b63d (905,988 XBP) is one of these rescues, not an exploit. trace_filter over all three deployments (blocks 10272668-12500000) finds no successful safeTransferFrom to a non-Bancor receiver before the anchor at index 1 of block 10287175.

Campaign: the 30 transactions (anchor included) with a successful safeTransferFrom whose from is neither the caller nor the receiver and whose receiver is not 0x29551fc9: 19 by bot 0x01da73c4 (all sent by EOA 0x052ede4c), 8 by bot 0x22f5c5e6 and 2 by 0xe929bcd4 (both reached through executor 0x9799b475), and 1 direct call by EOA 0xccf04c53; the last drain is 0x06b85bc6 (block 10568438).

Loss is the gross amount these callers took from approving users, priced at block time by loss.mjs, minus 311.57 BNT and 0.045 MKR that the bots' copies of Bancor's calldata sent to 0x29551fc9 inside campaign transactions. Unpriced RDN, HEDG and RPL are valued at the ETH the bots realised selling them on Uniswap v1 (1.5268, 0.4124 and 0.0301 ETH); AIX at 0. Bot 0x01da73c4 later returned the 92,297.6 AIX and 3,051,796.9 XBP to Bancor (0xf44518f0); recoveries are not subtracted (rule 11). Reported figures are about $135k taken by front-running bots and $409k rescued by Bancor.
